conflicts.about: Whether each transporter row gets Design Release 2.1's 'View details' link to the transporter's details, which DR1 left out until it was settled where the link would go.

positions.says: Leave the 'View details' link out until the address-book slice settles where it would go.
Each row has 'View details' to the transporter's address book view, returning to the transporter list.
On look and feel, the prototype (Design Release 2.1) wins by default over what the real services do today.
Which service owns transporter records, and where their details page lives, follow the real services.
The address book's transporter rows, the 'View details' link among them, are blocked with transporter management.
The address book is the system of record for transporters, which settles where a transporter's page lives.
Every row ends with a 'View details' link to that transporter's page in the INS address book, carrying the list's own URL back.

conflicts.outcome: Build Design Release 2.1's 'View details' link on each transporter row, with the transporter's name as visually hidden text and a return to the transporter list: the link is look and feel, which the prototype decides. Its destination is not the prototype's own path: the 9 October ruling left which service owns transporter records, and where their page lives, to the real services, and the 6 November ruling settles that it is the address book. DR1 (inc-122) only deferred the link until its destination was settled, so it is set aside. The block the 9 October afternoon ruling put on it is lifted with the rest of transporter management (c-285), and the link is already built: repo-frontend-p12-027 sends it to /address-book/transporter/{id} and repo-tests-p7-113 proves the round trip, so req-394 now exists rather than being new.

conflicts.about: Design Release 2.1 leaves the notification status block off 'Choose a transporter type' and 'Add a private transporter' but shows it on the transporter list and 'Add a commercial transporter'.

positions.says: 'Choose a transporter type' and the private transporter pages show no status bar, while the transporter details page and the commercial pages do.
'Add a commercial transporter' shows the notification status block.
Every page in today's transporter flow shows the journey strip.
The strip is shown on the transporter list and the commercial form and on neither the type question nor the private form.

conflicts.outcome: Follow Design Release 2.1 page by page: 'Choose a transporter type' and 'Add a private transporter' show no notification status strip, while the transporter list and 'Add a commercial transporter' keep it. The prototype wins by default; no DR1 judgement covers this difference and no persistence, validation, authentication or cross-service constraint is involved, so the strip the end-to-end traces show on every transporter page gives way. The animals frontend has since been built this way (repo-frontend-p12-074, repo-frontend-p13-054, repo-tests-p2-088), so req-427 exists. What the pages show once the address book serves them is a question of its own (c-390).

conflicts.about: The private transporter's country list: Design Release 2.1's countries, DR1's ruling that country lists come from MDM, and the 9 October ruling that every list is built now from reference-data as MDM serves it.

positions.says: The private transporter's country list is the UK plus reference-data's GBNAG_SPS_EX block, built now, never edited in code; where its content differs from Design Release 2.1, that is MDM's to change.
A parity finding whose fix is the content of a master reference-data list, countries included, is deferred to the MDM integration rather than built.
The private Country select holds 42 places: the EU member states and their outermost regions, the Crown Dependencies and the United Kingdom.
The private transporter's country list is blocked with transporter management, replacing the 9 October ruling's unblocking for it.
A private transporter is unaffected by the forced Northern Ireland country and keeps its real choice from the United Kingdom plus reference-data's export countries.
A reference list is MDM's content reaching the service through reference-data; it is never a reason to block a row and never edited in code.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October ruling outranks DR1 and the prototype on content: the list is the United Kingdom plus reference-data's GBNAG_SPS_EX countries, exactly as MDM serves them (req-432), and Design Release 2.1's different content (its regions, territories and Crown Dependencies) is MDM's to change, never edited in code (req-1818). The 6 November ruling confirms the private transporter keeps that choice, and the 11 November ruling confirms a reference list is never a reason to block a row. DR1's MDM judgement still stands for who owns list content, so it is not overruled; only its MDM block is lifted. Design Release 2.1's look and feel for the select still stands: a plain select with the United Kingdom default, no placeholder and no divider (req-431), which the animals frontend now does. The block the 9 October afternoon ruling added is lifted with the rest of transporter management (c-285).

conflicts.about: A commercial transporter posted with a country other than Northern Ireland: the prototype silently sets Northern Ireland, the real service refuses it.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, validation among them, overrides the prototype.
The server sets the country to Northern Ireland regardless of what is posted.
The commercial transporter add form refuses a tampered country value rather than correcting it.
A posted country other than Northern Ireland is refused as tampering, but an empty or absent one passes.

conflicts.outcome: The rulings rank first and let a real validation constraint override the prototype: a tampered country is refused with today's message rather than rewritten, and the 6 November ruling says so in terms. The refusal also covers a country posted empty or absent, which today's check lets through (req-455). Nothing is overruled: the prototype claim also states the fixed Northern Ireland country, which stands (req-454). Which service makes the check is a question of its own (c-389).

conflicts.about: How the add forms end: DR1 ruled pages reached from another page end with the primary button alone; Design Release 2.1 adds 'Cancel and return to dashboard'.

Both add pages have a secondary 'Cancel and return to dashboard' button.

DR1 never saw a cancel-to-dashboard control, so its judgement does not reach it and Design Release 2.1's 'Cancel and return to dashboard' is adopted. Nothing is overruled. The block the 9 October afternoon ruling put on it is lifted with the rest of transporter management (c-285), and the control is already built (repo-frontend-p13-055), so req-440 exists. The same forms read 'Cancel and return to address book' when the add began in the address book (req-462).

conflicts.about: The transporters the service ships and their statuses: DR1 held the two commercial records' status open for the register's owner, Design Release 2.1 seeds four commercial and four private transporters of its own, and the 6 November ruling parks the lot.

positions.says: Nothing other than a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint overrides the prototype.
Whoever owns the commercial transporter register must rule what status García Livestock Transport SL and J & G Campbell LTD may carry.

The eight transporter records the service ships are the approved transporters in an initial hardcoded form and are parked: the two commercial placeholders are not replaced with the design's four and the private records' addresses and approval numbers are not changed.
The shipped private transporter records' addresses and approval numbers are not changed.
No row may rest on the prototype's app/data files for what data a notification captures or which values a field offers, those files being demo fixtures.

conflicts.outcome: The 6 November and 11 November rulings rank first and reverse what this conflict adopted before.
